title: Open Receipt Format v0.10
description: Machine-readable schema for ORF v0.10 records. Use with any JSON Schema validator (ajv, jsonschema, gojsonschema, etc.). See spec/orf-v0.10.md for field semantics.

type.description: string: free-form text (v0.1 compat); uri: resolvable reference + failure condition; predicate: checkable expression

window_seconds.description: How long the falsifier window stays open; check before expiry

falsifier.description: What would prove this decision wrong — a string (v0.1 compat) or a typed object (v0.2+ preferred for automatic checkability).

idempotency_key.description: Prevents double-spend on retry — write intent receipt before acting

settled.description: false at write time (intent); update to true when confirmed

decision_id.description: Decision ID in the orchestrator's ledger, or an orf:// URI for cross-ledger sub-tasks; may reference decision, delegation, or reconcile records

status.description: Status of this sub-task; partial indicates the sub-task was itself an orchestrator with mixed results. Pending sub-tasks have no sub_outcome entry. See spec/orf-v0.9.md for normative treatment under each resolution_policy.

notes.description: Explanation for non-held status; SHOULD be present for partial sub-outcomes describing the mix of results

resolution_policy_enum.description: How to interpret aggregate counts to derive outcome.status. any_falsified_is_failure: one falsified sub-task → falsified; partial > 0 also → falsified (v0.8: partial implies component-level falsification). majority_held_is_success: held > falsified → held; held == falsified → undetermined; held < falsified → falsified; partial count excluded from this calculation (v0.8: document exclusion in outcome.notes). custom: implementor-defined; SHOULD document partial treatment in outcome.notes.

total.description: Total number of sub-tasks dispatched in this cycle (known at dispatch time; required even for checkpoint records)

held.description: Count of sub-tasks with status held

falsified.description: Count of sub-tasks with status falsified

undetermined.description: Count of sub-tasks with status undetermined

partial.description: Count of sub-tasks with status partial; held + falsified + undetermined + partial + (pending ?? 0) must equal total. v0.8 normative: under any_falsified_is_failure, partial > 0 SHOULD produce status: falsified; under majority_held_is_success, partial is excluded from the majority calculation.

pending.description: v0.9: Count of sub-tasks dispatched but not yet resolved. When pending > 0, the outcome record is a checkpoint (status: in_progress), not a final record. Extends the total invariant: total == held + falsified + undetermined + partial + pending. When absent, defaults to 0 and the v0.8 invariant holds unchanged.

resolution_policy.description: The *applied* policy — which policy was actually used when computing outcome.status from this aggregate breakdown. Records reality, not intent. New in v0.6; declared/applied distinction made explicit in v0.7.

sub_outcomes.description: Per-sub-task detail for resolved sub-tasks. In a checkpoint record (pending > 0), length equals total - pending (only resolved sub-tasks listed). In a final record (pending == 0), length should equal total.

orf_version.description: v0.1–v0.9 records are valid v0.10 (fully backward compatible)

id.description: Unique within the ledger; idempotency key for the receipt (not the action)

actor_agent.description: Identity of the agent taking the action

intent.description: Why: the goal this action serves

precondition_read.description: State actually observed before acting — not assumed, observed

decision_rule.description: Rule or policy in force at decision time — recorded now, not reconstructed later

action.description: What was done — specific enough to replay or audit

action_idempotency_key.description: Key for the side-effect boundary — distinct from the receipt id (different idempotency gates)

confidence.description: Agent's stated confidence [0..1] that the action achieves its intent — enables calibration

reconstruction_class.description: recomputable: can be rebuilt from still-available inputs (evictable); irrecoverable: original is irreplaceable (must be pinned)

resolution_policy.description: The *declared* policy — what the orchestrator intends to apply when aggregating sub-task outcomes. New in v0.5; declared/applied distinction made explicit in v0.7.

spend.description: Present when the action involves expenditure; null when none

artifacts.description: Paths or references to supporting artifacts; orf://{ledger-name}/{decision-id} is the recognized cross-ledger format

decision_id.description: The id of the resolved decision or delegation record

falsifier_observed.description: Did the falsifying condition occur? false=held; true=falsified; null=undetermined, partial, or in_progress

status.description: Derived from falsifier_observed: false→held; true→falsified; null→undetermined, partial, or in_progress. in_progress (v0.9): checkpoint record — aggregate.pending > 0, not final; use partial when aggregate shows held>0 AND falsified>0 in a final record

notes.description: Explanation or context; SHOULD record reason when aggregate.resolution_policy diverges from decision.resolution_policy, or when partial sub-outcomes are excluded from majority calculation

artifacts.description: Paths or references to supporting evidence; orf:// URIs are the recognized cross-ledger format

aggregate.description: Optional structured breakdown of sub-task outcomes for multi-tool/sub-agent cycles. Required when status is in_progress (checkpoint records must include aggregate.pending > 0).

orf_version.description: reconcile is a v0.2+ record type; v0.1 implementations do not emit it

open_decision_id.description: The id of the decision or delegation record being reconciled

world_state_read.description: What was actually observed in the world on waking — the authoritative crash-gap check

gap_detected.description: Did the agent find a gap between the pre-sleep receipt and actual world state?

resolution.description: completed: no gap; not_completed: safe to retry; ambiguous: do not retry without manual review. For partial prior outcomes, see reconcile guidance in spec/orf-v0.5.md.

prior_outcome_status.description: Optional. The status of the prior outcome record being reconciled. Makes reconcile reasoning self-contained. New in v0.5; in_progress added in v0.9 for reconciling after a checkpoint (incomplete) outcome.

notes.description: Explanation of resolution — required in practice when resolution=ambiguous

orf_version.description: delegation is a v0.3+ record type

delegated_intent.description: What the orchestrator instructed the sub-agent to do — the assignment, not just the tool name

delegate_ledger.description: orf:// URI for the sub-agent's receipt ledger; enables crash recovery by pointing to where B's receipts will appear

parent_decision_id.description: The orchestrator's own cycle or decision record that triggered this delegation

action_idempotency_key.description: Key for the invocation boundary — same semantics as in decision records

falsifier.description: Condition that would indicate the sub-agent failed to execute the delegated task

custody_reason_enum.description: Why the coordinator seat moved. seat_claimed: an empty seat was taken (epoch 0, or after dormancy). budget_low: holder handed off while it still had budget to write a clean handoff. budget_exhausted: holder was out of budget. voluntary: non-budget reason. unresponsive: seat taken from a holder that stopped responding. preempted_by_user: a human moved the seat. council_exhausted: no member eligible — to_agent is null and resume_at is required.

budget.description: The outgoing seat-holder's self-reported budget state at handoff time. Self-reported: ORF records what the holder claimed, not what the provider metered.

window_seconds.description: Length of the provider's rolling budget window (e.g. 18000 for a five-hour window)

remaining_fraction.description: Fraction of the window's budget still available [0..1]. Drives the succession rule.

resets_at.description: When this member's budget window rolls over and it becomes eligible again

unit.description: What the provider meters (e.g. "tokens", "requests", "messages"); advisory only

agent.description: Member identity; free-form, same trust model as actor_agent

role.description: coordinator: holds the seat. hand: executes delegated work and is seat-eligible. observer: never seat-eligible.

status.description: available: eligible for the seat. exhausted: out of budget until resets_at. unreachable: not responding. onboarding: joined but has not yet appended a conforming record to the council ledger, so not yet seat-eligible.

resets_at.description: When this member's budget window rolls over; the minimum across exhausted members determines resume_at

remaining_fraction.description: Fraction of budget remaining; the succession rule picks the eligible member with the greatest value

capabilities.description: Free-form capability labels; advisory only, not used by the succession rule

custody.description: v0.10: a receipt for movement of the coordinator seat between peer agents, or for the council going dormant. delegation is vertical (orchestrator to sub-agent); custody is horizontal (peer to peer).

orf_version.description: custody is a v0.10+ record type

council.description: Council name; scopes seat_epoch. Two councils may each have their own epoch 0.

seat_epoch.description: Strictly monotonic within a council: increases by exactly 1 per custody record. Fences the seat — only one record per epoch is valid, and on a conflict the first appended wins.

from_agent.description: The outgoing seat-holder. null is valid only at seat_epoch 0 with reason seat_claimed.

to_agent.description: The incoming seat-holder. Must differ from from_agent. null means dormancy: no member is eligible, reason must be council_exhausted, and resume_at is required.

roster.description: Council membership snapshot at handoff time. Required in practice for dormancy records, since resume_at is derived from it.

open_decisions.description: Decision, delegation, or outcome ids (or orf:// URIs) the outgoing holder opened and did not close. The incoming holder MUST write a reconcile record for every entry before dispatching any new delegation.

resume_at.description: Earliest moment work can resume: the minimum resets_at across exhausted roster members. Required when to_agent is null. This record is the wake trigger; a sidecar file is a cache of it, not the authority.

handoff_ledger.description: orf:// URI for the ledger the incoming holder writes to, when it differs from this one

notes.description: Explanation; SHOULD be present for reason unresponsive or preempted_by_user

falsifier.description: What would show the handoff failed — e.g. no successor record within a window, or the successor dispatching before reconciling open_decisions
